sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Shopify sells itself as the one place to run commerce everywhere people shop: online, in person, on social and now inside AI chats. AI and 'agentic' selling are the headline of its Fall '26 Edition.
keyPoints: Homepage promise: 'Dream big and build fast on Shopify. The world's best commerce platform.' The superlative has no evidence on the page.
The enterprise page leads with conversion and cost: up to 36% better conversion and 33% lower total cost of ownership.
The hero headline, 'Be the next AI all-star', does not say what a merchant gets; the sub-line and /start page do.

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: The navigation groups products by merchant job rather than by product name: build a website, sell anywhere, marketing and analytics, run your business, get paid, and extend Shopify.

rows: One-click checkout, sold as the best-converting one
In-person selling with hardware and a POS Pro add-on
Products appear and sell inside ChatGPT, Gemini and other AI chats
Marketplaces (Amazon, Walmart, eBay), social platforms and Google
Self-serve wholesale for manufacturers and distributors, on all plans from Basic
Campaigns, audiences, email and automation inside the admin

gaps: Payments, Shipping, Taxes and Finances and Funding pages were in the navigation but not opened.

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: Four published monthly plans with a cheaper yearly price, a card rate that falls as the plan rises, one add-on and a $0 plan for AI channels. Trial terms are worded differently on different pages.
keyPoints: Pricing page entry offer: 3 days free, then $1 a month for 3 months. The channels page says 'free for 3 days, no credit card required'.
Every plan returns 1% of sales as subscription credit (0.5% on non-Shopify Payments).
POS Pro is a $89 a month add-on; the POS page pairs it with a hardware offer worth $2,400.
The Agentic plan is $0 a month, takes cards from 2.9% + 30¢ online, and you pay only when you make a sale.
gaps: App, theme and domain costs were not on the page.
Third-party payment gateway fees were not shown.

sections.title: Merchandising
sections.summary: The most deliberate offer ladder of the three. Every rung lowers a different kind of risk, and the top plan keeps a reason to move up.
keyPoints: Entry offer, yearly saving and a sales rebate paid as subscription credit each address a different hesitation.
Each plan names its buyer and its bullets start 'Everything in' the plan below; a compare-all-features link and a yearly toggle sit above the cards.
Fully customizable checkout is held back for Plus; POS and AI channels are sold as an add-on and a $0 pay-per-sale plan.
For merchants: Shopify Catalog structures product data for AI discovery, and checkout supports discounts, gift cards, pre-orders and subscriptions.
Not surveyed: collections, on-site search and recommendation tools.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: A separate developer site (shopify.dev) with docs for apps, storefronts and agents, a CLI and an AI toolkit. Apps can extend the admin, online store and checkout. The API reference itself was not opened.
keyPoints: Apps extend the admin, online store, checkout and more.
Storefronts can be custom themes or Hydrogen.
A section covers building agentic shopping experiences, and an AI toolkit connects coding assistants to the docs, API schemas and CLI.
The B2B page points to APIs for ERP integration.
The Fall '26 Edition is described as opening the catalog, cart and checkout to any agent or app.
gaps: No API reference, rate limits or webhook pages were read.

sections.title: Design
sections.summary: The most art-directed of the three: near-black backgrounds, full-bleed video, very large type and pill buttons, held together by one typeface. The cost is weight, and a hero that leads with mood over message.
keyPoints: One type family (Shopify-Inter) runs across the home page, pricing and signup; the docs use Inter.
Buttons are full pills (9999px corners) on the home and signup pages, and the header is sticky.
The home page opens on a full-bleed video with a 96px headline, and carries 15 videos in total.
Pricing keeps the dark theme: four dark plan cards, a yearly toggle at top left and a centered headline.
For merchants: AI store generation, prebuilt themes, Hydrogen, a customizable checkout and developer theme tools.
gaps: Light mode and the admin UI were not assessed.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: The newsroom frames Shopify as a network that grows with every connected AI agent. No About or customer-stories page surfaced from the navigation.
keyPoints: Newsroom narrative: Shopify was built to work wherever people shop, and every connected AI agent is a new place to sell.
Product news arrives in twice-yearly 'Editions'; Fall '26 is the current one.
Headline stats conflict: the checkout page says 12% of US ecommerce, the Agentic Storefronts page says 14%.
The conversion claim (15% better on average, up to 36%) cites a study from April 2023 by an unnamed consulting firm.

jtbd_fit.evidence: The nav groups products by merchant job (build, sell anywhere, market, run, get paid) and the signup path says 'Choose a design, add products, get paid'.

capability_visible.evidence: Checkout customizer, AI store builder and POS are demonstrated in-page; docs are public. The admin itself is behind signup.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Four plans with monthly and yearly prices, card rates and add-on are published. Trial terms differ between pricing and channels pages and app, theme and domain costs are absent.

product_breadth.evidence: Job-based nav is easy to read and new lines (Sidekick, Agentic Storefronts) are explained in plain language.

platform_depth.evidence: shopify.dev docs, CLI, AI toolkit, Hydrogen, apps in admin and checkout, agent docs. API reference was not read.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops at the account form.

friction.evidence: One click from home to /start, which asks for an email first and opens with theme choice.

trust.evidence: Merchant domains shown and a Forrester B2B leader mention, but no named customer stories page was found.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: Hero headline is abstract ('Be the next AI all-star'); the subhead and the /start page are clearer.

proof_quality.evidence: The 15% conversion lift cites a 2023 study by an unnamed consultancy, and US ecommerce share is 12% on one page and 14% on another.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: 'Start for free' is the CTA but the pricing page says '$1/month for 3 months' after 3 days; terms sit on different pages.

cta_logic.evidence: 'Start for free' is consistent in nav and body, with 'Talk to sales' for enterprise on B2B and Agentic pages.

company_narrative.evidence: The agentic-commerce story runs from homepage to newsroom to developer docs to a dedicated product page.

offer_packaging.evidence: Four plans each name a buyer, bullets build on the plan below, and a compare-all-features link and a yearly toggle sit above them.

offer_architecture.evidence: A $1 trial, yearly saving, sales rebate as credit, POS add-on with a hardware offer, a $0 pay-per-sale plan, and a top plan that unlocks checkout customization.

merchant_merch_tools.evidence: Catalog, discounts, gift cards, pre-orders, subscriptions, channels and marketing tools are shown. Collections and search were not surveyed.

visual_craft.evidence: Distinct and consistent: dark theme, one typeface, huge headline, pill buttons. Heavy on video (15 on the home page) and the hero headline does not say what the product does.

system_coherence.evidence: Same family from home to docs to signup and the same pill buttons; docs use a muted accent.

merchant_design_control.evidence: AI store generation, themes, Hydrogen, a customizable checkout and developer theme tools are all shown.

read.summary: A job-organised catalogue with a transparent plan ladder, now reframed around AI and agentic selling. Strong on breadth and pricing, weaker on named proof and on consistent trial terms.
pros: Nav and /start both explain Shopify by merchant job, not product name.
Plan ladder is public, with a clear monthly vs yearly saving and falling card rates.
A $0 'Agentic' plan lets a merchant try AI-channel selling and pay per sale.
Developer site, CLI and AI toolkit are public and linked from the main nav.
cons: The hero headline is abstract; the plain-language promise is in the subhead.
Trial terms differ: 'free for 3 days, no credit card' vs '$1/month for 3 months'.
Headline stats conflict (12% vs 14% of US ecommerce) and the conversion study is dated and unnamed.
No About or customer stories page surfaced.
read.howItSells: Sells momentum and reach: sell everywhere, build fast, AI built in. Backs it with checkout conversion stats and a long plan ladder with a low-commitment start.
copy: Group the product nav by the merchant's job.
Offer a pay-per-sale plan for a new channel.
State monthly and yearly prices side by side.
avoid: Different trial terms on different pages.
A headline stat that changes between pages.
unknowns: API reference depth and rate limits.
Costs for apps, themes, domains and third-party payment gateways.

hypothesis.statement: Stating one trial term (3 days free, then $1/month for 3 months) next to every 'Start for free' button will cut post-signup billing surprise without lowering signup starts.
hypothesis.metric: Signup start rate and day-3 paid-conversion rate
hypothesis.guardrail: Refund and support-contact rate in the first week
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if starts hold within 2% and week-one billing contacts fall over a two-week split.

merchandising.summary: A real ladder with a reason for every rung. The offer is merchandised more cleverly than Stripe's or Klaviyo's, and merchants are given discounting, pre-order and subscription tools to do the same.
pros: Every plan names its buyer and builds on the one below.
The entry offer, yearly saving and sales rebate each lower a different kind of risk.
A $0 pay-per-sale plan lowers the barrier to a new channel.
Checkout customization is held back as a reason to move up.
cons: The trial terms differ between pricing and channels pages.
Hardware discount and POS add-on require reading two pages.
No collections or search tooling was shown.

design.summary: The most art-directed of the three. The system holds from marketing to docs to signup. The cost is weight and a hero that leads with mood over message.
pros: One typeface, one button shape and one dark theme are held across pages.
Merchants are offered AI, themes, Hydrogen and a customizable checkout.
Plan cards are easy to compare.
cons: The home hero headline does not say what Shopify does.
Fifteen videos on the home page.
Dark cards give plan text lower contrast than a light theme would.

claims.text: Shopify's overall conversion rate outpaces the competition by up to 36% and by an average of 15%, based on a study completed in April 2023 in partnership with a Big Three global management consulting company.
Try Shopify free for 3 days, no credit card required.
Shopify sites render up to 2.4x faster than stores on other platforms and 1.8x faster on average.

signupPath: 'Get started fast' leads to shopify.com/start. That is a long landing page (a theme picker, how-to videos and trial terms: '3 days free', 'Extend your trial for $1') with a single email box near the bottom and a line saying you agree to receive Shopify marketing emails. No password, name or store details are asked on this page. What comes after the email was not reached.
